skill.name: executing-plans

content.value_statement: Large implementation plans can drift without checkpoints. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through batch execution, verification, and review pauses.
actual_capabilities: Loads and reviews a provided implementation plan before starting work.
Executes tasks in default batches of three items.
Marks tasks as in progress and completed during execution.
Runs verification steps that the plan explicitly requires.
Reports batch results and waits for review before continuing.
Stops when blockers, unclear instructions, or major plan gaps appear.
limitations: Requires a complete implementation plan from the user or another skill.
Does not design the plan or choose architecture by itself.
Depends on the available project tools and test commands.
Needs human feedback between batches when review is requested.

use_cases.title: Implement a Prepared Feature Plan
use_cases.description: A developer provides a finished plan and wants controlled execution with tests after each task.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Review Checkpoints
use_cases.description: A technical lead wants batch summaries before the next group of changes begins.

use_cases.title: Run Structured Maintenance Work
use_cases.description: A maintainer uses the skill to process refactors, fixes, or cleanup tasks without losing task status.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a Simple Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a clear plan file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use executing-plans to run the implementation plan in docs/plan.md. Work in batches and stop after each batch for review.

prompt_templates.title: Run With Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan includes required test or build steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute this plan in batches of three tasks. Run every verification step listed in the plan and report the result before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Blockers Carefully
prompt_templates.scenario: Complex work may reveal missing dependencies or unclear steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use executing-plans on the provided plan. Stop immediately if a blocker, unclear instruction, or major plan gap appears.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Batch Delivery
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with review gates and follow-up changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute the plan across multiple batches. After each batch, summarize completed tasks, verification results, risks, and required architect feedback.

output_examples.input: Execute the plan for a three-task bug fix batch.
output_examples.output: Batch 1 complete. Task 1 fixed the failing validation path. Task 2 updated the related test coverage. Task 3 confirmed the build and test checks passed.

output_examples.input: Continue after review feedback changes one task.
output_examples.output: Feedback applied. The affected task was updated, verification was rerun, and the next batch is ready for review before execution.

output_examples.input: A plan step depends on a missing package.
output_examples.output: Execution stopped because a required dependency is missing. The next action is to confirm the dependency choice before continuing.

best_practices: Provide a complete plan with tasks, expected changes, and verification steps.
Review each batch summary before asking the assistant to continue.
Use clear stopping rules for blockers, unclear instructions, and failed checks.
anti_patterns: Starting with a vague goal instead of a concrete implementation plan.
Skipping verification steps that the plan requires.
Continuing across review checkpoints without reading the batch summary.

faq.question: Does this skill write implementation plans?
faq.answer: No. It executes an existing plan. Use a planning workflow first if the plan is not ready.

faq.question: What is the default batch size?
faq.answer: The documented default is three tasks per batch before reporting and waiting for feedback.

faq.question: Can it run tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It follows verification steps that the plan explicitly lists, such as tests or builds.

faq.question: When should execution stop?
faq.answer: It should stop for blockers, unclear instructions, critical plan gaps, or failed required verification.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is human review required between batches?
faq.answer: The workflow expects a report and feedback checkpoint before the next batch begins.
